place.source_title: Western Springs Water Tower, 914 Hillgrove Avenue

brief: Masonry standpipe water tower of 1892: a round rough-cut limestone base with an arched entrance up stone steps, a tall brick cylinder above with long recessed arched panels, and a projecting bracketed cornice at the top. Stands in a small park with planters. Record: 3 Commons photos plus 10 HABS measured drawing sheets.

facade.notes: the Western Springs IL water tower (1892): a masonry standpipe -- a rough-cut limestone drum with arched windows and an arched door, a red-brick upper cylinder with recessed arched panels, a corbelled cornice under a broad conical roof; now a museum in a small park with lamp posts and paths at the village centre

why.note: every town's water tower: height gives the mains their pressure, so the tower stands on the highest ground and becomes the town's landmark
